articles.headline: Street-car exclusion items (Philadelphia)
articles.summary: 'Conductor, has the Car Run off the Track?' -- On Thursday evening last, four colored gentlemen entered one of the street cars on Pine street which did not bear the sign 'Colored Persons admitted.' The conductor requested them to get out; they refused, politely but emphatically; he feared to use force, as the law would not permit it. Most of the white passengers seemed satisfied with their remaining. The conductor, as a last resort, with the driver's help, worked several minutes running the car off the track; the colored gentlemen remained in the car; the horses were unhitched and taken to the stable; a crowd collected and many white persons applauded the colored men for this assertion of their rights. Separately, under 'Suit for Damages,' a highly respectable colored lady of this city has entered suit against one of the street railroad companies for forcible ejectment from one of their cars. (No individuals named.)

events.name: New Year in Philadelphia -- public meeting at Bethel Church to celebrate the abolition of slavery
events.description: On New Year's night (Jan. 1, 1866) a public meeting was held in Bethel Church to celebrate the abolition of slavery in the United States. On motion, Rev. William Moore was appointed Chairman and Rev. Stephen Smith Vice President; Prof. Bassett and Mr. A. Fields were appointed Secretaries. Rev. Jacob Mitchel made remarks while a committee drew up resolutions expressive of gratitude to Almighty God for the abolition of slavery; resolutions were also passed on the loss of Dr. McCune Smith of New York. After remarks by the editor, Bishop Campbell spoke nearly half an hour; Mr. Bowers and Dr. Armstrong also spoke. A committee -- Prof. Bassett, Rev. Stephen Smith, Wm. Whipper, A. Fields and the editor -- was appointed to draw up an address to the President and Congress on the right of franchise. (Thirteenth Amendment / Emancipation celebration.)

events.name: A Grand Concert and Organ Exhibition -- Shiloh Baptist church
events.description: On the 25th ultimo (Dec. 25, 1865) a concert was held at the Shiloh Baptist church, of which the late Rev. J[eremiah] Asher was pastor. The concert was given by Professor Lively; the organ was built by a colored gentleman by the name of Joseph Carter, who does business in South Street, Philadelphia (eight stops; compass from gg to Alt., 54 notes). Mr. Lively was assisted by Professors W. A. Newton and another (name obscured by ink/damage). The concert was opened by Rev. Mr. Miller of Pearl Street Baptist church.

events.name: Emancipation Celebration -- Pearl Street Baptist church
events.description: A special service in commemoration of the total abolition of slavery in the United States, held at the Pearl Street Baptist church, Sunday evening last, Dec. 31st, 1865. After introductory exercises and an anthem, the Pastor, Rev. T. Doughty Miller, read the proclamation of Hon. Wm. H. Seward (Dec. 18th) announcing the amendment abolishing slavery; a discourse on Numbers 16 followed, eulogizing the brave colored volunteers. A preamble and resolutions were adopted by the congregation (thanks to Congress, the Cabinet, the ratifying States and the Union press; copies ordered sent to President Andrew Johnson, Hon. Wm. H. Seward, Hon. Charles Sumner, Hon. Wm. D. Kelly and Hon. Thaddeus Stevens). (Thirteenth Amendment celebration.)

events.name: Meeting of Colored Citizens of Philadelphia -- Philadelphia Institute (SCSA lectures announced)
events.description: Adjourned meeting of the Colored citizens of Philadelphia, held in the Philadelphia Institute, Wednesday evening, Jan. 3d, 1866 (the 6th of a weekly series). Richard H. Gleaves, President; J. B. Young and J. W. Purnell, Secretaries. On motion of U. B. Vidal, after remarks by Messrs. Vidal, Hubert, Catto, Stephen Smith, Still, J. C. Bowers and J. W. Brown, it was resolved that the colored citizens of Philadelphia recommend to the people of Pennsylvania that William Whipper, Esq., of Columbia, be appointed to represent and urge forward their interests at the National Capitol during the present session of Congress. On motion of E. D. Bassett it was further resolved to pledge aid to Mr. Whipper. The Secretaries were directed to lay the proceedings before the city pastors. A subscription list opened, amounting to eighty dollars ($80). Rev. Stephen Smith and Mr. William Still announced that a course of public lectures was soon to open at Concert Hall under the auspices of the 'Social, Civil and Statistical Association of the Colored People of Pennsylvania' (SCSA), and that Hon. Charles Sumner and other eminent persons had accepted invitations to lecture. Adjourned to Jan. 10th.

events.name: Episcopal Meeting of the A.M.E. Bishops (Philadelphia)
events.description: The Bishops of the A.M.E. Church met in Philadelphia on the 4th of January, 1866, to confer with the General Book Steward (Rev. E. Weaver) and the Trustees of the Book Concern as to its financial condition. The Book Steward's account showed that a large and commodious building had been purchased for the Book Concern at a cost of three thousand five hundred dollars ($3,500). On Rev. E. Weaver's communication asking for assistance in conducting the affairs of the Book Concern and the Christian Recorder, the Board resolved to grant the request and appointed Rev. James Lynch Editor of the Christian Recorder. A communication from the Quarterly Conference of Bethel Church, Philadelphia, requested the Bishops to issue an address to the colored citizens of the United States upon their duties as citizens and Christians; granted. events.description: The A.M.E. Church will complete its fiftieth year on April 16, 1866. Harper ('The Nation's Great Opportunity'); March 8, Prof. Wm. H. Day; March 15, Hon. Wm. D. Kelley. The Committee hoped to add Maj. Gen. B. F. Butler and Rev. H. W. Beecher. Tickets for the course (six lectures) $1.50; single 25 cents; to be had at Pugh's, 6th and Chestnut. Miss E. T. Greenfield (the Black Swan) kindly volunteered to furnish appropriate music each evening. Committee of Arrangements: William Still, Chairman; U. B. Vidal; Jacob C. White, Sr.

events.name: Meeting of the Annual Conferences (1866 schedule)
events.description: The time and place of the meeting of Conferences and their presiding Bishops: Ohio Conference, April 3, Chillicothe, O., Bishop Quinn; Baltimore Conference, April 10, Washington, D.C., Bishop Payne; South Carolina Conference, May 2, Charleston, S.C., Bishop Payne; Philadelphia Conference, May 23, Princeton, N.J., Bishop Wayman; New England Conference, June 17, New Bedford, Mass., Bishop Quinn; New York Conference, June 20, New York City, Bishop Wayman; Indiana Conference, Aug. 9, Quincy, Ill., Bishop Campbell; Missouri Conference, Aug. 23, St. Louis, Mo., Bishop Campbell; Louisiana Conference, Oct. 4, New Orleans, La., Bishop Campbell.

events.name: Banneker Colored School of Kingsessing -- donation to the freedmen
events.description: 'A Worthy Example': a contribution of ninety cents from the pupils of the Banneker Colored School, of Kingsessing, for the purpose of alleviating the sufferings of the many refugees (freedmen). The editor hopes other schools will follow the example.

events.name: Zoar M.E. Church Sabbath School -- twenty-fourth anniversary
events.location: Zoar Methodist Episcopal Church, Brown street above Fourth, Philadelphia
events.description: The Zoar Methodist Episcopal church, in Brown street, above Fourth -- or rather, the Sabbath School connected therewith -- will celebrate their twenty-fourth anniversary on Sabbath next, the 11th instant, at 3 o'clock P.M. Brother William H. Thomas, the tried and worthy Superintendent of the School, has spared no pains to make the celebration fully up to the standard of its predecessors.

events.name: Bethel Sunday School -- resignation and election of superintendent
events.description: Bethel Sunday school has made a change recently. Brother Lewis Seymour (L. B. Seymour), for years the superintendent and long engaged in the training of the youth of Bethel Church, has resigned, carrying the good wishes and prayers of all. William C. Heston, a young man brought up in the school and long its secretary, of unblemished character and employed in the (A.M.E.) book store, has been elected to fill Bro. Seymour's place.
attendees: resigned Superintendent of Bethel Sunday School
elected Superintendent of Bethel Sunday School

events.name: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League -- organizing of auxiliary leagues in Bucks County (Attleborough)
events.location: Bucks County, Pa. (Attleborough and other townships)
events.description: A correspondent ('Progress') describes visiting Bucks Co., Pa., and attending meetings in several townships called to form Equal Rights Leagues. The people of the county had invited Messrs. Foster and Catto, members and agents of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League, to explain the aims and objects of the association. At the Attleborough meeting (over forty present), an officer of the church introduced Mr. Foster, of Philadelphia, who delivered an address urging union, suffrage, morality, education, temperance and industry; the Attleborough league now has some forty members. The gentleman from Philadelphia's province is to inaugurate these auxiliary leagues; communities so organized have established night schools, reading circles and debating societies.
attendees: agent of the Penn'a State Equal Rights League (printed as surname; likely O. V. Catto)
agent of the Penn'a State Equal Rights League, of Philadelphia (printed as surname)

events.name: Grand Exhibition -- Sabbath School of the Union A.M.E. Church
events.description: A Grand Exhibition by the Sabbath School of the A.M.E. Union Church, to take place at that church on Wednesday and Thursday evenings, the 21st and 22d insts. (Feb. 21-22, 1866). Mr. A. Harris is the trainer of the children for the occasion. Rev. R. P. Gibbs, the pastor of the church, and Mr. James B. Turner, Superintendent of the school, beg the patronage of the public. Tickets for the two entertainments, 40 cents.
attendees: trainer of the children for the exhibition

events.name: Grand Lodge of Pennsylvania (A.Y.M., Prince Hall) -- St. John's Day installation of officers
events.description: St. John's Day, Philadelphia, Dec. 27th, A.D. 1865 (A.L. 5865). At the Annual Grand Communication of the M.W. Grand Lodge for the State of Pennsylvania, A.Y.M. (Prince Hall / African York Masons), the brethren elected and re-elected on Monday Dec. 25th, 1865, were installed for the ensuing Masonic year. Grand officers: Nathaniel L. Durham, M.W. Grand Master; Ralph G. Gilmore, R.W. Dep. Gr. Master; George Woolford, R.W. Sen. Gr. Warden; George Roper, R.W. Jun. Gr. Warden; John G. Dutton, R.W. Grand Treasurer; Alfred S. Cassey, R.W. Grand Secretary; Wm. Shipley, Sen. G. Deacon; Joseph W. Cassey, Jun. G. Deacon; Moses Jones, G. Marshal; Jas. S. Hollowell, G. Sword Bearer; Wm. A. K. Smith, G. Standard Bearer; Peter Tunnel, G. Bible Bearer; Saml. B. Collins, G. Master of Ceremonies; Peter Parkes, G. Pursuivant; Peter Mitchell, G. Tyler; Benj. Harrison, Sen. G. Steward; Henry O'Donnell, Jun. G. Steward. Grand Chaplains: Rev. Bros. R. Faucett, Wm. G. Cooper, and J. Frisbey. Grand Lecturer: R.W. Bro. Fred. O. Revels. District Deputy Grand Masters: Samuel M. Bennett (Harrisburg), Charles H. Vance (Harrisburg), Thos. Early (Harrisburg), Hannibal G. Molson (Lewistown), Wm. Nesbit (Altoona), Archibald J. Billows (Pittsburgh), George B. Vashon (Pittsburgh), David Leary (Philadelphia, for Montgomery and Bucks), John Dean (Philadelphia, for Lehigh, Northampton, Carbon and Luzerne), James T. Robinson (Philadelphia, for Delaware and Chester). Committees -- Landmarks: Wm. H. Riley, S. Van Brakle, J. Needham, H. Shadd, Wm. E. Gipson, R. H. Gleaves, J. Davis M.D. (with the M.W.G.M. and R.W.D.G.M.). By-Laws: B. B. Moore, F. R. Brolasques, T. MacPherson. Correspondence: T. MacPherson, E. Y. Venning, J. W. Page, Jas. W. Cassey, T. Charnock. Finance: P. N. Judah, S. Durham, Wm. Cooper, S. Downing, T. D. Jordan, E. Mathews, C. H. Edwards. G.L. Charity Fund: T. MacPherson, J. C. Green, R. Cauff, H. Clarke, J. G. Miller, L. Dennis, J. C. Miller. Ways and Means: S. B. Collins, T. Charnock, G. Boston, Nathl. Morgan, G. W. R. Hall, Wm. Allen, T. Cline, E. A. Rudolph, Wm. King. Appeals: J. Needham, F. R. Brolasques, U. Kelley, E. Carney, Geo. Brown. Grievances: H. Shadd, D. G. Cornish, D. G. Clarke, Joseph Doyer, B. B. Moore. Attest, Alfred Cassey, R.W.G. Secretary.

D.D.G. Master, of Philadelphia (Lehigh, Northampton, Carbon, Luzerne)
D.D.G. Master, of Philadelphia (Delaware and Chester)
Committee on By-Laws, Correspondence, Charity Fund
Committee on Correspondence and Ways and Means

events.name: Old Folks' Concert for the Zion A.M.E. Mission Church
events.location: Philadelphia (concert to be repeated at Sansom St. Hall)
events.description: Rev. Henry J. Rhodes reports that the Zion A.M.E. Mission Church (of this city -- a page-2 note confirms Rhodes is pastor of the Zion Mission Church in this city and teaches a public school in Germantown) was financially embarrassed. Mrs. S. Rhodes proposed an Old Folks' Concert for the church's benefit; Brother Wm. G. Cooper moved to rent a hall, carried. Mrs. Rhodes secured the assistance of: Miss J. Jones, Mr. D. and Mrs. B. Shockley, Mr. B. and Mrs. M. Syers, Mrs. R. Dade and S. Butler, Mrs. E. Ates and Turner, Miss E. Hollis, P. Henson, M. and S. Dickerson, Messrs. J. Jones, J. Graham, S. Jones, J. Cannon, A. Syers, M. Handley, T. Jones, G. Ates, Mr. Shockley, Mr. Jones and Mr. Brown; Mr. A. Barres presided at the organ and Mr. Gaiter conducted the singing. The concert took in $126.07 (expenses $45). A committee of Mrs. S. Rhodes, Mrs. A. Johnson and G. Jones presented $81.07 to the Trustees. The association proposes to repeat the concert on the 14th of March, at the Sansom St. Hall.
attendees: moved to rent a hall for the concert

events.name: Sermon to Young Men at Bethel Church, by Rev. James Lynch
events.description: A special sermon to young men will be delivered at Bethel Church, on Sunday evening, the 25th inst., at half past 7 o'clock, by Rev. James Lynch. Subject -- 'What am I born for?'
attendees: preacher (Rev.; the new editor of the Christian Recorder)

events.name: Bishop Jabez P. Campbell in Philadelphia (collation to friends)
events.description: Bishop Jabez P. Campbell is still in Philadelphia and will not leave (for the West) for about three weeks. The Bishop gave a fine collation to many of his friends on Saturday afternoon.

events.name: Celebration of Bishop Allen's birthday at Bethel Church
events.description: A celebration of Bishop Allen's birthday was held at Bethel Church of this city on Wednesday evening of last week (Feb. 14, 1866), at which Mr. John Jones (of Illinois, the Washington suffrage delegate) delivered an address. (The surrounding article recounts the Indiana Annual Conference proceedings and the origin of the Washington colored delegation; John Jones is not a Philadelphian and is not linked.)

events.name: Protracted meeting commenced at Bethel Church
events.description: A protracted meeting has commenced at Bethel Church. Bishop Campbell preached, on last Monday evening, a discourse which exhibited great demonstration of Divine power; several penitents went to the altar.
attendees: preached the discourse (Bishop; = J. P. Campbell)

events.name: Excelsior Base Ball Club -- reorganization and election of officers
events.description: At a meeting held on Friday evening, Feb. 9th, 1866 (notice dated Philadelphia, Feb. 19, 1866), a reorganization of the Excelsior Base Ball Club was effected, and the following officers elected for the ensuing year: J. H. Francis, President; Francis Wood, Vice President; J. Field Needham, Recording Secretary; Edwin Johnson, Corresponding Secretary; Daniel Holden, Treasurer. Directors: Frisby Stevens, George W. Scott, John Brace.

events.name: Ladies' festival at Pennington, N.J. (Trenton Circuit)
events.description: The ladies of Pennington, N.J., held a festival on Thursday and Friday evenings, Feb. 1st and 2d, 1866, and realized therefrom, clear of all expenses, the sum of $35, $30 of which was paid over to the minister. Committee: Mary Watson, Hannah Moore, Caroline Caby, Hannah Allen. Reported by Thos. H. Cooper. (The committee women are of Pennington, N.J.; recorded in the description.)

events.name: A.M.E. Semi-Centenary Celebration -- Philadelphia district plan and committees
events.description: The 50th anniversary (Semi-Centenary) of the organization of the A.M.E. Church. By published arrangements of the Bishops, the 8th, 15th and 16th days of April 1866 are set apart for religious services and collections (education, missionary, book concern, worn-out preachers). The amount to be raised in the district is $15,309 (membership 5,103; three dollars per member). Appeal 'To the members of the Philadelphia and New York Conference' signed A. W. Wayman (127 S. [--] St.). Committees as printed: Publishing Committee -- Rev. S. L. Hammond, W. D. W. Schureman, George T. Watkins. Central Committee, Itinerant -- S. L. Hammond, Jno. M. Brown, G. T. Watkins, D. W. Moore, B. T. Tanner, W. D. W. Schureman, Jno. J. Herbert, Jas. D. T. Hall; Layman -- W. H. G. Brown, Charles Hicks, Lloyd Benson, Arthur Smith, Clement Becket, Thomas E. Green. LAY COMMITTEE: Philadelphia -- William Scott, Charles Simpson, Abram Fields, Francis P. Main, N. Chase; Princeton, N.J. -- James Schenck; Wilmington, Del. -- D. P. Hamilton; Salem, N.J. -- Joseph Gibbs; Camden, N.J. -- Aaron Mackey; Mount Holly, N.J. -- Charles Sulsey. William Moore, Chairman of the Committee (Phila., Jan. 30th). A parallel appeal for the same celebration was issued from the Missouri District by Wm. R. Revels (St. Louis).
attendees: bishop; issued the Philadelphia & New York Conference appeal

events.name: Lecture at Concert Hall -- C.S.S. Association lecture course (Gen. Carl Schurz)
events.description: The third lecture of the C.S.S. Association [Social, Civil and Statistical Association] lecture course was delivered on Thursday evening last by Gen. Carl Schurz. On the platform were several gentlemen connected with the Pennsylvania Freedman's Relief Association: Bishop Campbell of the A.M.E. Church; Rev. Stephen Smith; James Powell, Esq.; Robert [Davis?], Esq., and others. Miss E. T. Greenfield and Miss Freeman treated the audience to music. The lecturer was introduced by Mr. Isaiah O. Weare. Schurz advocated negro suffrage, opposed the readmission of the states lately in rebellion, and criticized the President.

events.name: Concert and Exhibition at Union Church (Sabbath School)
events.description: A Concert and Exhibition at Union Church, by the Sabbath School, held two nights this week, was a grand success; the attendance was large and composed of highly respectable persons. The recitations and dialogues were given with good effect and the music was above the average. The teachers and superintendent deserve great credit. Mr. A. Barris presided at the meeting and as usual made every one feel at home and happy.

events.name: Bethel Sabbath School Concert
events.description: The concert of the Bethel Sabbath school, held on the 8th of February at Concert Hall, was well attended and highly successful. The singing warranted the highest praise upon the scholars and their excellent instructor, Mr. Hans Shadd, whose untiring exertions, with the committee of arrangements, made the concert a success.
attendees: instructor of the Bethel Sabbath school

events.name: Preachers' Meeting of the travelling and local preachers of Philadelphia and vicinity
events.description: The Preachers' Meeting, composed of the travelling and local preachers in Philadelphia and vicinity, was well attended last Tuesday. A discussion took place on the question: Was the external man concerned, in common with the internal, according to the Biblical acceptation of the terms? In the affirmative were Rev. William Moore, Rev. B. P. Eddy, Rev. Josiah Eddy; in the negative were Bishop J. P. Campbell and Rev. Stephen Smith. Rev. W. D. W. Schureman entered into the discussion with great spirit. The decision seemed to be, 'There was no decision.'

events.name: Old Folk's Concert for the benefit of the Book Concern
events.description: Notice: 'Help the Book Concern.' Go to the 'Old Folk's Concert,' at Sansom Street Hall, next Tuesday evening, 13th inst.; proceeds to aid the Book Concern of the A.M.E. Church.

events.name: Tribute of Respect for Rev. Jonathan C. Gibbs -- Seventh Street Presbyterian Church
events.location: lecture room (Benezet Hall), Seventh Street Presbyterian Church, Philadelphia
events.description: At a congregational meeting of the members of the Seventh Street Presbyterian Church, held at their lecture room, Benezet Hall, on Friday evening, March 2d, 1866, for the purpose of responding to the request of Rev. Jonathan C. Gibbs to the Philadelphia Presbytery for permission to resign his pastoral relations with his congregation (to labor among the freedmen). Mr. Alexander Guy was called to the chair, and Mr. Nathaniel W. Depee appointed secretary. Mr. Joseph C. Bustill presented the preamble and resolutions, which, on motion of Mr. J. C. Farbeaux, were unanimously adopted (acquiescing in the Pastor's request and tendering him sympathy). Messrs. Joseph C. Bustill and William Scull were appointed commissioners to convey the resolutions to the Presbytery. Phila., March 1[2]th, 1866.

events.name: Dedication of the Institute for Colored Youth
events.description: The Dedication of the Institute for Colored Youth took place on Friday, the 9th inst., at 11 o'clock. The new building is three stories high, fifty-one by eighty feet, cost nearly fifty thousand dollars, divided into male and female departments, with a reading room, library, laboratory and apparatus rooms. Program: Opening remarks by M. C. Cope, Sec'y of the Corporation; Address by Wm. Evans, Jr., a member of the Board of Managers; a poem by Miss Fannie M. Jackson, Principal of the Female Department; Remarks by E. D. Bassett, Principal of the Institute; Oration by O. V. Catto, teacher in the Institute; Essay by Miss C. B. Le Count, of the class of 1866; Dissertation by J. H. Davis, of the Senior Class; Dissertation by Sarah F. Iredell, of the Junior Class; a dialogue by a class of small boys and a recitation by a class of small girls.
attendees: Secretary of the Corporation; opening remarks
member of the Board of Managers; address
Principal of the Female Department; poem

events.name: Election of members to the Social, Civil and Statistical Association of Pennsylvania
events.description: Dr. David Rosell, Rev. James Lynch, and W. C. Bantum were recently elected members of the Civil, Social and Statistical Association of Pennsylvania (the S.C.S.A.).

events.name: The Minister that has the Most Friends -- Fair for the Christian Recorder (silver pitcher vote)
events.description: The ladies preparing to give the fair for the benefit of the Christian Recorder are to present a silver pitcher to the minister receiving the highest number of votes, irrespective of denomination. The ministers listed: Rev. Mr. Hamer of Brick Wesley; Rev. J. Mitchell of Little Wesley; Rev. Mr. Allston of St. Thomas church; Rev. William Moore of Bethel church; Rev. Mr. Reeves of (Central) Presbyterian church; Rev. T. D. Miller of Pearl St. Baptist church; Rev. R. P. Gibbs of Union church; Rev. Henry J. Rhodes of Zion church; Rev. Elisha Weaver, General Book Steward; Rev. James Lynch, Editor of the Christian Recorder.
attendees: pastor of Pearl St. Baptist church (Rev.)

events.name: Presentation at Bethel Church
events.description: At Bethel church, the presentation of a gift was made by Miss L. Boyer (a student); a speech was given by Rev. Stephen Smith, and the gift replied to by returning thanks on behalf of the committee. (Report continues from the missing page 2.)

events.name: Grand Fair of the Union Baptist Sabbath School
events.location: Union Baptist Church, Minster Street above Sixth, Philadelphia
events.description: A Grand Fair for the sale of Useful and Fancy Articles will be given at (for the benefit of) the Union Baptist Sabbath School, to be held at the Union Baptist Church, Minster Street above Sixth, commencing on Easter Monday evening, April 2d, 1866, and continuing during the week, to purchase a new set of books and library for the school. Admission: single tickets 10 cts., season tickets 25 cts., to be had of any of the teachers or scholars.

events.name: Quarterly Meeting of the Rt. Rev. Bishop D. A. Payne Association
events.location: Philadelphia Institute, Lombard St. below 7th, Philadelphia
events.description: Notice: The regular stated Quarterly Meeting of the Rt. Rev. Bishop D. A. Payne Association will be held on Monday evening, the 26th, at the Philadelphia Institute, Lombard St., below 7th, at 8 o'clock. Signed A. E. Teagle.

events.name: Zion A.M.E. Mission Church -- last Quarterly Meeting of the Conference year
events.description: Notice: The last Quarterly Meeting for the conference year of Zion A.M.E. Mission Church will be held April 1st, 1866, at which time the stated pastors of the A.M.E. Church in this city and vicinity are expected, also Revs. Jas. Lynch and E. Weaver. Signed H. J. Rhodes, Pastor.
attendees: pastor of Zion A.M.E. Mission Church (Rev.)

events.name: Garnet League (Equal Rights) reading-room dedication, Harrisburg
events.description: The Garnet League of Harrisburg. Rev. H. H. Garnet, of Washington City, lectured on the 19th ult. (subject, 'The secret of success in life'), under the auspices of the League. On the same evening the reading-room belonging to the institution was opened, Rev. Mr. Garnet delivering a dedicatory address; the room was filled with members of the League and friends, prominent among whom were members of 'Cleveland's Concert Troupe,' Mrs. Elizabeth Berra and Mrs. Bella Tilghman, of Philadelphia; Mrs. Carrie Johnston and Miss Missouri Hall, of Allegheny; Mr. Cupit, of York; and others. On the 21st the room opened to the public and the ladies presented, through Rev. Mr. Garnet, a splendid Bible to the League, received on its part by Prof. Wm. Howard Day. Also present: Sergt. Rufus Jones, of the 8th U.S.C.T., J. C. Bustill, J. C. White, and David Houser, of Philadelphia. Many books donated (Shakespeare, Josephus by Chaplain David Stevens). Membership now 250.

events.name: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League
events.description: We have been favored by Jacob C. White, Jr., Esq., with a copy of the preamble and constitution of this League. It acts under the jurisdiction of the National Equal Rights League of the United States of America, and has its office at 717 Lombard Street, Philadelphia. The solicitors are Mr. Joseph C. Bustill, No. 403 South Sixth Street, Phila., and Mr. O. C. L. Hughes, Harrisburg, who are the officers appointed to give information to persons in any part of the state desiring to form auxiliary leagues. William Nesbit, Esq., is the President; Prof. G. B. Vashon and Mr. O. V. Catto, Secretaries; Mr. James Needham, Treasurer. The League has forty-three auxiliaries scattered throughout the state, and recently presented a memorial to Congress stating the grievances of the colored people of the state (treated with respect by the Senate; published in full by the Morning Chronicle of Washington).

events.name: School for the Colored Blind
events.description: Notice: A school for the colored blind exists in this city, taught Monday and Thursday afternoons of each week at the Institute, commencing at 5 o'clock P.M. No charge whatever is made. Those having blind children or friends should send them.

events.name: A.M.E. Wesley Church -- appointments for Sabbath, April 1st
events.description: Notice: Appointment for Sabbath, April 1st, 1866, in the A.M.E. Wesley church, Philadelphia, Pa. -- 10 1/2 o'clock A.M., E. Weaver; 2 o'clock P.M., P. P. Main; 7 o'clock P.M., Thomas Williams.
